Images and sources of the (proto)Physics PhD Thesis: TOE - Quantum Cosmology (except private sources): TOE - Quantum Cosmology: Unifying quantum mechanics with Einstein's general relativity, the measurement problem and other important fundamental problems of physics. Contextual implications (epistemological and ontological vision of reality and its different contexts). 

I affirm that the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics is incapable of deriving objective probabilities and Born's rule without falling into circular arguments, and on the other hand, that current cosmological models, such as inflationary or cyclical ones, are an epistemological and incomplete vision of reality, each presenting its own problems, without being able to incorporate quantum gravity and where the hypothesis of the block universe fails, causing the appearance of infinities. However, with a quantum cosmology model, and with a universal wave function with a closed time curve (CTC), and that applies Everett's interpretation, all these problems disappear, offering a complete, objective and ontological vision of universe, which gives rise to a model of a block universe, spatially finite, without edges, and apparently static, which provides an ontological vision to the meaning of the arrow of time and probabilities within the framework of quantum mechanics. Furthermore, it is combined with current theories that try to solve the problem of quantum gravity, privileging a type of discrete space-time. This “quantum multiverse” model manages to connect with relativistic cosmological models through the MWI=Cosmological Multiverse hypothesis, applying a holographic method and the principle of complementarity, emerging both space-time and the Born rule naturally. I show that without a theory of hidden variables and superdeterminism, this model is the only way to reconstruct determinism due to the measurement problem, and if it is not true, reality is intrinsically indeterminate and there is no arrow of time without appearance of infinities. Only a hidden variable interpretation could represent a model similar to the one presented here, but it would inevitably be superdeterministic and would entail a series of problems that show that Bohm's interpretation is a many-worlds-in-negation interpretation. Furthermore, both in single universe models and in cyclical or inflationary models, it is shown that Bohm's interpretation is not capable of reproducing the existence of a single possible world, even when the initial conditions during the birth of each universe are the same, either during a big bounce or the birth of bubble universes or "creation ex nihilo", which is a highly restrictive and unlikely scenario.
